response: Anorectal endosonography is indeed valuable in the diagnosis of dyschesia. Linear anorectal endosonography has been shown to demonstrate incomplete or absent relaxation of the anal sphincter and the m. puborectalis during a defecation movement in the majority of patients with dyschesia. This technique is particularly useful in highlighting "pelvic floor dyssynergia" or "anismus", making it a valuable tool in the diagnosis of dyschesia.
